situationBrief.title: Repairing Class 10 Assembly Notices
situationBrief.description: Wind scattered the notices for the Class 10 Science and Heritage Exhibition across the courtyard. Help Mira, Arjun, and Gyan rebuild every message.

storyIntro.sceneTitle: Scattered Exhibition Notices in the Courtyard

beats.speaker: mira
beats.dialogue: Our Class 10 morning assembly board lost half its cards in the wind! Only scattered phrases remain on the pins.

beats.speaker: arjun
beats.dialogue: This strip only reads '... plays cricket.' Without knowing who we are speaking about, the notice cannot communicate a full clause.

beats.speaker: gyan
beats.dialogue: To restore every notice accurately, let us pair each Subject head-noun with its finite-verb Predicate. Ready to rebuild the board?

grammarOutcomes: Identify full Subjects, head-words, and Predicates across simple and enlarged Class 10 sentences.
Spot finite verbs inside Predicates and recognise understood '(You)' in imperatives.
See how Predicates extend into Verb + Object or Verb + Complement patterns.
learningObjectives.knowledgeOutcome: Explore Indian scientific, agricultural, and historical contexts through accurate sentence structure.

sourceReferences.bookTitle: Learn and Practise Grammar Class - X
sourceReferences.note: Builds on Class IX Subject/Predicate knowledge to analyse finite verbs and SV, SVO, SVOO, SVC, SVOC patterns.

sourceReferences.bookTitle: LEARN AND PRACTISE GRAMMAR CLASS - IX
sourceReferences.chapter: Chapter 1: Parts of a Sentence (Sections A & B)
sourceReferences.note: Class IX foundational Subject/Predicate definition, head-words, and understood 'you' in imperatives.

sourceReferences.bookTitle: A NEW METHOD English Grammar For Class IX & X

Original courtyard mission narrative and Subject/Predicate bridge for Class 10 learners, since Odisha Class X assumes this foundation from Class IX.

sentences.title: Core Model Sentence
sentences.note: Clear SVO (Subject + Verb + Object) model connecting Class 9 basics with Class 10 clause patterns.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Determiner opening the Subject noun phrase.
Head-word of the Subject; controls the singular finite verb 'plays'.
Finite verb beginning the Predicate 'plays cricket'.
Direct Object inside the Predicate (S + V + O pattern).

groups.label: Subject
groups.textbookRule: A simple sentence contains one finite clause made of a Subject and a Predicate containing the finite verb (Assam IX-X Ch. 1 p. 3; Odisha X Ch. 2 p. 13).

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What is said about the subject?
groups.textbookRule: In an S + V + O pattern, the finite verb and its object together form the Predicate (Odisha Class X, Ch. 2, pp. 14-15).

relationships.label: Determiner → Head-Noun
relationships.explanation: 'The' specifies the head-noun 'boy' inside the Subject.

relationships.label: Adjective → Head-Noun
relationships.explanation: 'little' modifies 'boy' before the finite verb begins.

relationships.label: Head-Noun ↔ Finite Verb
relationships.explanation: The singular head-noun 'boy' determines the singular finite verb 'plays'.

sentences.title: Guided Discovery Sentence
sentences.note: Requires learners to locate the Subject and compound finite verb phrase ('are reading') before viewing the explanation.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Plural noun naming who is doing the action.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Plural head-noun governing the finite auxiliary 'are'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shows present continuous time and plural agreement.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Starts the Predicate right after the Subject.
Pairs with 'are' inside the finite Predicate.
Direct Object completing the S + V + O Predicate.

groups.label: Subject
groups.textbookRule: The Subject names the person or group spoken about before the finite verb begins (Assam IX-X Ch. 1 p. 2).

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What is said about the students?
groups.plainExplanation: 'are reading books' is the Predicate containing the verb group 'are reading' + Direct Object 'books'.
groups.textbookRule: In S + V + O clauses, the finite verb phrase and object together make up the Predicate (Odisha Class X, Ch. 2, pp. 14-15).

relationships.label: Head-Noun ↔ Finite Verb
relationships.explanation: Plural head-noun 'students' governs the finite auxiliary 'are' inside 'are reading'.

structureSummary.patternNote: Subject + Verb Phrase + Direct Object (S + V + O)

sentences.title: Class 10 Comparison
sentences.rawText: The diligent students in Class 10 read science books.
sentences.note: Demonstrates an enlarged Subject with a prepositional modifier ('in Class 10') governing a plural finite verb ('read').

tokens.meaningInSentence: Points to the specific group of students.
Names the plural group doing the reading.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Head-word of the Subject; it is plural ('students'), not singular.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Introduces which class the students belong to.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Starts the post-modifier 'in Class 10' inside the Subject.
Plural finite verb starting the Predicate 'read science books'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Tells what kind of books they read.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'The diligent students in Class 10' is the complete Subject, with 'students' as its head-word.
groups.textbookRule: Prepositional phrases following a noun stay inside the Subject; the head-noun ('students') governs the finite verb (Assam IX-X Ch. 1 pp. 3-6; Odisha IX Ch. 1 p. 6).

groups.label: Predicate
groups.textbookRule: The Predicate starts at the finite verb 'read' and includes the Direct Object 'science books' (Odisha Class X, Ch. 2, pp. 14-15).

relationships.label: Post-modifier → Head-Noun
relationships.explanation: 'in Class 10' specifies which 'students', staying inside the Subject before the verb.

relationships.label: Head-Noun ↔ Finite Verb
relationships.explanation: Plural head-noun 'students' (not 'Class 10') locks onto the finite verb 'read'.

teachingSequence.title: Understand the Complete Sentence
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Words combine in S + V + O order to share one clear clause.
teachingSequence.explanation: 'The little boy plays cricket.' communicates a complete message. Tap any word to see its role and meaning.

teachingSequence.title: Discover the Subject
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Ask: Who are we talking about?
teachingSequence.explanation: 'The little boy' forms the complete Subject group before the finite verb begins.

visualCallout.question: Who are we talking about?
visualCallout.label: 'The little boy' (Head-Noun: 'boy')
visualCallout.detail: 'boy' is the Subject head-noun controlling the singular finite verb 'plays'. Without the Subject, the clause has no anchor.

teachingSequence.title: Understand the Subject's Meaning
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Spotting the true Subject head-noun prepares you for Agreement and Tenses.
teachingSequence.explanation: 'The' and 'little' modify 'boy', keeping the whole phrase anchored as the Subject.

teachingSequence.title: Discover the Predicate
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Ask: What is said about the little boy?
teachingSequence.explanation: 'plays cricket' is the Predicate. It starts at the finite verb 'plays' and includes the Direct Object 'cricket'.

teachingSequence.title: Understand the Complete Structure
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Subject ('The little boy') + Predicate ('plays cricket') = complete S + V + O clause.
teachingSequence.explanation: Pinned together on the noticeboard, Subject and Predicate express a complete, grammatical statement.

guidedChallenge.promptSubject: Step 1: Tap the Subject in 'The students are reading books.'
guidedChallenge.promptPredicate: Step 2: Now tap the Predicate (include the auxiliary 'are' + main verb + object).
guidedChallenge.subjectFeedback: Select who the clause speaks about before the finite auxiliary verb 'are': 'The students'.
guidedChallenge.predicateFeedback: Begin at the finite auxiliary verb 'are' and include 'reading' and 'books'.
guidedChallenge.unlockedExplanation: Accurate! 'The students' is the Subject, and 'are reading books' is the Predicate (Verb Phrase + Direct Object).

teachingSequence.title: Explore Another Example
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Identify Subject and Predicate first to reveal the structural analysis.
teachingSequence.explanation: Try locating both parts in 'The students are reading books.' before inspecting the breakdown.

teachingSequence.title: Enlarged Subjects & Agreement Bridge
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Post-modifiers after a noun stay inside the Subject.
teachingSequence.explanation: Compare with 'The diligent students in Class 10 read science books.' Notice plural 'students' (not 'Class 10') governs 'read'.

wordLabActivities.title: A. Identify Subject & Predicate
wordLabActivities.instruction: First tap all words in the complete Subject, then tap all words in the Predicate.

sentence.title: Exhibition Notice
sentence.rawText: The young athletes from Manipur win medals every year.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Main noun naming who the sentence is about.
Links the athletes to their state.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Starts the post-modifier inside the Subject.
Starts the Predicate 'win medals every year'.

wordLabActivities.correctFeedback: Excellent! 'The young athletes from Manipur' is the enlarged Subject, and 'win medals every year' is the Predicate.
wordLabActivities.incorrectSubjectFeedback: Include the post-modifier 'from Manipur' because it tells which athletes we mean—stop right before the finite verb 'win'.
wordLabActivities.incorrectPredicateFeedback: Select all words from the finite verb 'win' through 'year.' to form the Predicate.
wordLabActivities.hint: Find the finite verb ('win') first; everything before it belongs to the Subject, and everything from 'win' onward is the Predicate.

wordLabActivities.title: B. Categorise Subject & Predicate Clauses
wordLabActivities.instruction: Assign each notice strip to Subject or Predicate.

categories.label: Subject
categories.helperText: Who or what the statement is about

items.explanation: Noun group with head-word 'engineers' and modifier 'in Bengaluru' — no finite verb yet.
items.hint: Noun group with head-word 'engineers' — there is no finite verb yet.

items.explanation: Begins with the finite verb 'designed' + Direct Object.
items.hint: Look at the first word: 'designed' is a finite action verb.

items.text: A balanced meal of rice, dal, and greens
items.explanation: Names the healthy meal being discussed.
items.hint: Names the meal being talked about — no finite verb is included.

items.explanation: Begins with the linking verb 'is' + Subject Complement.
items.hint: Begins with the linking verb 'is' describing the Subject.

sentencePairs.subjectText: A balanced meal of rice, dal, and greens

wordLabActivities.completeFeedback: Accurate work! You separated both action (S+V+O) and linking (S+V+C) Predicates cleanly from enlarged Subjects.

wordLabActivities.title: C. Construct an Accurate Heritage Sentence
wordLabActivities.instruction: Arrange these tiles to form a clear sentence with Subject first and Predicate second.
wordLabActivities.promptContext: Hint: Who is the sentence about, and what finite verb starts the Predicate?
wordLabActivities.correctFeedback: Well structured! 'Rani Lakshmibai' (Subject) + 'defended Jhansi with courage.' (Predicate: Verb + Object + Adverbial).
wordLabActivities.incorrectFeedback: Start with the Subject ('Rani Lakshmibai'), followed by the finite verb ('defended'), object ('Jhansi'), and manner ('with courage.').

wordLabActivities.title: D. Replace the Finite Verb & Observe Shift
wordLabActivities.instruction: Swap the verb 'plays' in 'The little boy plays cricket.' to see how the Predicate changes meaning while keeping agreement.

options.meaningEffect: Means the boy actively takes part in the game.
options.roleImpactNote: Singular finite verb matching 'boy' in the Predicate.

options.meaningEffect: Shifts the meaning to regular training and skill-building.
options.roleImpactNote: Remains a singular transitive finite verb taking the object 'cricket'.

options.meaningEffect: Focuses on the boy's appreciation of the sport.
options.roleImpactNote: Still agrees with the singular head-noun 'boy' inside the Subject.

wordLabActivities.takeaway: Replacing the finite verb transforms what the Predicate says about the Subject while preserving the S + V + O pattern.

wordLabActivities.title: E. Supply the Missing Predicate
wordLabActivities.instruction: Select the option with a finite verb to complete this science notice.
wordLabActivities.sentenceBeforeBlank: Clean drinking water from the filter

options.feedback: Without a finite verb like 'is', 'stored in covered steel vessels' is only a participial modifier—not a full Predicate.

options.text: keeps every student hydrated during assembly
options.feedback: Correct! The finite verb 'keeps' agrees with the singular head-noun 'water' and completes the Predicate.

options.text: for all Class 9 and Class 10 rooms
options.feedback: This prepositional phrase has no verb, so it cannot act as a Predicate.

wordLabActivities.title: F. Diagnose the Structural Error
wordLabActivities.instruction: Identify what makes this assembly draft ungrammatical.
wordLabActivities.brokenSentence: The science models prepared by Class 10 students.
wordLabActivities.repairedSentence: The science models prepared by Class 10 students won first prize.
wordLabActivities.question: Why is 'The science models prepared by Class 10 students.' incomplete?

options.label: 'prepared' is a past participle modifier, so the sentence has no finite verb / Predicate.
options.feedback: Exact diagnosis! 'prepared by Class 10 students' modifies 'models' inside the Subject. Adding a finite verb such as 'won first prize' creates the Predicate.

options.label: 'students' cannot appear at the end of a sentence.
options.feedback: Nouns can appear at the end of sentences. The issue is that no finite verb states what happened to the models.

options.label: A sentence cannot begin with 'The'.
options.feedback: Determiners like 'The' commonly open Subjects; the missing part here is the Predicate.

independentPractice.cueText: Light cue: 'Rice and dal' work together as a compound Subject before 'give'.
independentPractice.title: Balanced Lunch Notice
independentPractice.instruction: Select the Subject first, then select the Predicate.

sentence.title: Independent Sentence 1
sentence.rawText: Rice and dal give steady strength to growing students.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: First part of the compound Subject.
Joins both nouns inside the Subject.
Completes the plural compound Subject 'Rice and dal'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shows what rice and dal provide.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Plural finite verb starting the Predicate.

structureSummary.predicateText: give steady strength to growing students

independentPractice.successFeedback: Accurate! 'Rice and dal' is the compound Subject governing the plural finite verb 'give'.
independentPractice.retrySubjectFeedback: Select all three words 'Rice and dal' before the finite verb 'give'.
independentPractice.retryPredicateFeedback: Select every word from the finite verb 'give' through 'students.'.

independentPractice.cueText: Spot the linking verb ('is') to divide the enlarged Subject from its S+V+C Predicate.
independentPractice.title: Morning Health Advisory
independentPractice.instruction: Tap the complete Subject, then tap the complete Predicate.

sentence.title: Independent Sentence 2
sentence.rawText: A balanced breakfast with fresh fruit is essential before school.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Main noun naming what we talk about.
Adds detail about what is in the breakfast.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Starts post-modifier 'with fresh fruit' inside the Subject.
Starts the S + V + C Predicate.

structureSummary.subjectText: A balanced breakfast with fresh fruit

independentPractice.successFeedback: Well done! 'A balanced breakfast with fresh fruit' is the enlarged Subject (head-noun 'breakfast'), and 'is essential before school' is the Predicate.
independentPractice.retrySubjectFeedback: 'with fresh fruit' modifies 'breakfast' inside the Subject—stop right before the linking verb 'is'.
independentPractice.retryPredicateFeedback: Start at the linking verb 'is' and include 'essential before school.'.

independentPractice.title: Science Exhibition Card
independentPractice.instruction: On your own: separate the complete Subject from the Predicate.

sentence.title: Independent Sentence 3
sentence.rawText: ISRO scientists in Bengaluru launched the weather satellite.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Names the people doing the action.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Completes the S + V + O Predicate.

independentPractice.successFeedback: Clean analysis! 'ISRO scientists in Bengaluru' is the enlarged Subject, and 'launched the weather satellite' is the S+V+O Predicate.
independentPractice.retrySubjectFeedback: Keep 'in Bengaluru' attached to 'ISRO scientists' inside the Subject before 'launched'.
independentPractice.retryPredicateFeedback: Select from the finite verb 'launched' through 'satellite.'.

independentPractice.title: Exhibition Duty Card
independentPractice.instruction: Examine this imperative notice and choose the accurate structural analysis.

sentence.title: Imperative Notice
sentence.rawText: Check every notice on the board carefully.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Opens the Predicate when 'You' is understood.

structureSummary.predicateText: Check every notice on the board carefully

independentPractice.imperativeQuestion: How do Subject and Predicate work in this imperative clause?

imperativeOptions.label: 'every notice' is the Subject because it is a noun phrase.
imperativeOptions.feedback: 'every notice' receives the action of checking—it is the Direct Object inside the Predicate.

imperativeOptions.label: The Subject is understood '(You)', and 'Check every notice on the board carefully.' is the Predicate.
imperativeOptions.feedback: Spot on! Imperative sentences omit the spoken Subject '(You)' while retaining a complete Predicate starting with the verb 'Check' (Odisha IX Ch. 1 p. 7; Odisha X Ch. 2 p. 13).

imperativeOptions.label: An imperative sentence has no Predicate.
imperativeOptions.feedback: An imperative sentence starts directly with its finite verb ('Check'), making the spoken command a complete Predicate.

independentPractice.successFeedback: Strong grasp! You recognised the understood '(You)' Subject in an imperative sentence.

completionSummary.headline: Class 10 Noticeboard Restored!
completionSummary.celebrationMessage: Mira, Arjun, and Gyan have pinned every repaired notice back on the courtyard board. You mastered Subject, Predicate, and finite verbs across simple and enlarged sentences!
learnedPoints: A complete clause pairs a Subject (who/what we talk about) with a Predicate containing a finite verb.
Prepositional modifiers after a noun stay inside the Subject, while the Subject head-noun controls the finite verb.
Imperative notices keep an understood '(You)' Subject and express the Predicate starting directly with the verb.
repairedMessages: ISRO scientists in Bengaluru launched the weather satellite.
Check every notice on the board carefully.
completionSummary.rewardLabel: Class 10 Structure Star & Balanced Harvest Badge
